item.text: I’m taking another pass through the remaining UI and reader classes. The goal is still a behavior-preserving refactor with clear structural payoff, not just stylistic churn.

I found a solid refactor seam in `MenuView`: the form-building and form-reading code still threads a lot of state through parameters and duplicates choice-selection logic. I’m cleaning that up into a more self-contained UI object now.
The menu refactor is in. I’m compiling now and checking for any unused constants or rough edges from the helper extraction.
There’s one leftover cleanup in the menu refactor: I introduced a spacing constant and hadn’t wired it through yet. I’m fixing that and then I’ll close this pass out.
I’m running the final compile for this pass now.

I refactored [MenuView.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R005_module_java/MenuView.java:15) into a more self-contained UI component. The main changes were making its state fields `final`, moving repeated UI literals into constants, collapsing the separate habitat/scenario combo-box builders into one labeled-choice helper, and removing parameter-threading for `animalNumberReceivers` by having the form read its own fields directly.

I also tightened the input path so the form-reading methods work on `List` interfaces throughout, and extracted a shared `getSelectedItem(...)` helper to avoid duplicating combo-box access logic. This keeps the menu logic flatter and makes the class easier to modify without chasing state through multiple helper signatures.

Verification: `javac *.java` passes.
